name: Refund processing
description: Compiled from one recorded execution in Northstar Support.
goal: Issue a refund to a customer

rules.statement: "create refund" must happen before "add audit note"

provenance.detail: the operator did createRefund, then addAuditNote

implications: An agent that does them the other way round will fail.

question.text: Must "create refund" always come before "add audit note"?
question.reason: That was the order in the recording. It may simply have been convenient.

rules.statement: every refund must record who did it

question.text: Must every refund record who performed it?
question.reason: The field can be left empty, and the operator filled it in once.

rules.statement: the refund's amount must equal the refund's manager approval requested amount

provenance.detail: in the demonstration the refund's amount and the refund's manager approval requested amount were both 82

implications: An agent that lets the two differ will fail.

question.text: Must the refund's amount always equal the refund's manager approval requested amount?
question.reason: They matched once. One recording cannot show whether a mismatch is ever allowed.

then.describe: the refund's amount equals the refund's manager approval requested amount

rules.statement: the refund's amount must not exceed the refund's order total

provenance.detail: in the demonstration the refund's amount was below the refund's order total

implications: An agent that goes over will fail.

question.text: Must the refund's amount never exceed the refund's order total?
question.reason: One recording stayed below the other value; nothing showed what happens above it.

then.describe: the refund's amount is at most the refund's order total

rules.statement: the refund's manager approval requested amount must not exceed the refund's order total

provenance.detail: in the demonstration the refund's manager approval requested amount was below the refund's order total

implications: An agent that goes over will fail.

question.text: Must the refund's manager approval requested amount never exceed the refund's order total?
question.reason: One recording stayed below the other value; nothing showed what happens above it.

then.describe: the refund's manager approval requested amount is at most the refund's order total

rules.statement: the refund's manager approval manager must not be the refund's issued by

provenance.detail: in the demonstration the refund's manager approval manager and the refund's issued by were deliberately different

implications: An agent that lets one person do both halves of the job will fail.

question.text: Must the refund's manager approval manager always be someone other than the refund's issued by?
question.reason: One recording shows one pairing. Whether it is a rule was never demonstrated.

then.describe: the refund's manager approval manager is not the refund's issued by

rules.statement: the refund's customer id must be the refund's order customer id

provenance.detail: in the demonstration the refund's customer id and the refund's order customer id were the same

implications: An agent acting on a record belonging to someone else will fail.

question.text: Must the refund's customer id always be the refund's order customer id?
question.reason: One recording shows one pairing. Whether it is a rule was never demonstrated.

then.describe: the refund's customer id is the refund's order customer id

rules.statement: the refund's customer id must be the refund's support ticket order customer id

provenance.detail: in the demonstration the refund's customer id and the refund's support ticket order customer id were the same

implications: An agent acting on a record belonging to someone else will fail.

question.text: Must the refund's customer id always be the refund's support ticket order customer id?
question.reason: One recording shows one pairing. Whether it is a rule was never demonstrated.

then.describe: the refund's customer id is the refund's support ticket order customer id

rules.statement: the refund's order id must be the refund's support ticket order id

provenance.detail: in the demonstration the refund's order id and the refund's support ticket order id were the same

implications: An agent acting on a record belonging to someone else will fail.

question.text: Must the refund's order id always be the refund's support ticket order id?
question.reason: One recording shows one pairing. Whether it is a rule was never demonstrated.

then.describe: the refund's order id is the refund's support ticket order id

rules.statement: every refund must be linked to a support ticket

provenance.detail: the demonstration linked a support ticket

implications: An agent that completes the job without a support ticket will fail.

question.text: Does every refund always need a support ticket?
question.reason: One recording linked a support ticket. Whether it is mandatory was never demonstrated.

rules.statement: every refund must be recorded in an audit entry

provenance.detail: the demonstration wrote an audit entry naming the new refund

implications: An agent that does the work but records nothing will fail.

question.text: Must every refund be written to the audit entry?
question.reason: The operator did it once. Whether it is required was not demonstrated.

rules.statement: the refund's manager approval status must be "approved" when the work is done

provenance.detail: the linked record was "approved" when work began

implications: An agent acting on a record in another state will fail.

question.text: Must the refund's manager approval status always be "approved" for this work to be allowed?
question.reason: The recorded case happened to be "approved". It could also be "pending" or "rejected", and none of those were exercised.

then.describe: the refund's manager approval status is "approved"

rules.statement: the refund's order status must be "delivered" when the work is done

provenance.detail: the linked record was "delivered" when work began

implications: An agent acting on a record in another state will fail.

question.text: Must the refund's order status always be "delivered" for this work to be allowed?
question.reason: The recorded case happened to be "delivered". It could also be "processing", "shipped" or "cancelled", and none of those were exercised.

rules.statement: the refund's support ticket status must be "open" when the work is done

provenance.detail: the linked record was "open" when work began

implications: An agent acting on a record in another state will fail.

question.text: Must the refund's support ticket status always be "open" for this work to be allowed?
question.reason: The recorded case happened to be "open". It could also be "pending_customer", "resolved" or "closed", and none of those were exercised.

then.describe: the refund's support ticket status is "open"

rules.statement: when the refund's amount is above $50, it must carry a manager approval marked approved

provenance.detail: Refunds of $50 or less can be issued without approval.
the demonstrated value was $82, with a manager approval marked approved

implications: Above it, an agent that proceeds without a manager approval marked approved will fail.

question.text: When the refund's amount is above $50, must it carry a manager approval marked approved?
question.reason: RigorRun read "Refunds of $50 or less can be issued without approval." in the interface. That is text on a page, not a policy source of truth, and one recording shows one amount.

rules.statement: at most one refund per manager approval

provenance.detail: the demonstration created exactly one refund

implications: An agent that creates a second refund for the same manager approval will fail.

question.text: Could there ever legitimately be a second refund for the same manager approval?
question.reason: Only one was created in the recording, which does not show whether a second is allowed.
question.counterexample: A partial or follow-up refund would be a second one for the same manager approval.
